summary: Verify against tron source when the AMX path runs under FPGA attention (decode + prefill), refute every claim, synthesize cases

kept.text: In apply_page_tok, begin and end are not the CPU-required sub-range of the page: begin is 0 (1 only for EAGLE) and end is page.count(), the number of live entries of the page, with no input from the query mask.
kept.evidence: `size_t begin = 0;` ... `if (k_position == 0 && q_position != 0) begin = 1;` ... `size_t end = page.count();` ("page.count() tracks active entries during traversal, skipping stale entries from other branches")
corrections: Precise wording: "In apply_page_tok, begin and end are page-level bounds, not the query's required sub-range. begin is 0, and becomes 1 only when the model is EAGLE, the page's first token is at position 0, and the query is not at position 0 [self_attention.hpp:1726-1739]. end is page.count(), which returns offset_bound = the number of live entries on the page as fixed by compute_forward_args before the forward [self_attention.hpp:1743; kv_cache.hpp:1483-1494]. The query mask (range_hint, query_visible, sw_required) does not change begin or end; it only decides, inside the dotter loop, which offsets in [begin, end) are scored [self_attention.hpp:1746-1747, 1792-1803]."

Precise wording: begin is 0 except for EAGLE models, where it is 1 only on the page whose first entry is position 0 and only when the query position is not 0 [self_attention.hpp:1732-1739]; end is page.count() = offset_bound, the number of live entries on this page as set by compute_forward_args via set_offset_bound (usually 64 for internal pages, fewer for the leaf page or after branch-then-delete) [kv_cache.hpp:1483-1494]. The query mask never narrows begin/end; it only sets query_visible, which the dotter loop uses to skip ranges and which is_dense_amx_page consumes as a separate argument [self_attention.hpp:1746-1747, 1760-1761, 1795-1804].

kept.text: A full page that contains the HW/SW boundary has begin == 0 and end == 64, but it fails is_dense_amx_page because query_visible is evaluated once on the range of the page's first token, and under FPGA attention that first range is the card's range where sw_required(job_ix) is false.
kept.evidence: `bool query_visible = run_visible_in_software ? range_hint->visible(job_ix) : range_hint->sw_required(job_ix);` and `return begin == 0 && end == page::page_size && query_visible && ...`; the shard event does `masks.sw_mask() = {}; masks.hw_mask() |= offloadable;` so entries at or below the boundary carry the query only in HW_AVAILABLE
corrections: A full page that contains the HW/SW boundary has begin == 0 and end == 64 but fails is_dense_amx_page on two independent conditions: (1) query_visible is computed once, before the AMX gate, from the range of the page's first token (page_begin_hint, self_attention.hpp:1471-1472, :1746-1747), and under FPGA attention that range is the card's range, where the offloaded query sits only in hw_mask so sw_required(job_ix) is false (ranged_mask.cpp:67-73, :82; ranged_mask.hpp:160-162); (2) the card range's tok_hi is the boundary+1, which is at or below the page's last token, so `pg.at_offset(63) < range.tok_hi` is also false (self_attention.hpp:1610). On a sliding-window layer (run_visible_in_software true, :1406-1407) query_visible is visible() and is true, and only condition (2) excludes the page. The dotter loop then scores the SW tail of that page on AVX (:1793-1804).

A full page that contains the HW/SW boundary has begin == 0 and end == 64 but fails is_dense_amx_page on two conjuncts at once. First, query_visible is evaluated once on the range of the page's first token (page_begin_hint = find_range(page.at_offset(0)), self_attention.hpp:1471-1472, passed at :1541, read at :1746-1747); in a hardware layer (run_visible_in_software false, :1406-1407) that range is the offloaded range, where the job sits only in hw_mask (ranged_mask.cpp:67-70), so sw_required(job_ix) is false (ranged_mask.hpp:160-162). Second, and independently, that range ends at the boundary token + 1, which is inside the page, so pg.at_offset(63) < range.tok_hi is false (self_attention.hpp:1609-1610). The query_visible reason applies only to layers with uses_hw true and no sliding window (compute_operation_uses_hw, :487-495); in a sliding-window layer query_visible = visible(job_ix) is true in the offloaded range (ranged_mask.hpp:155-157) and the boundary page fails only through the tok_hi conjunct. Either way the page falls to the dotter loop, which advances the hint at the boundary (:1793-1798) and scores the SW-required tail on AVX.

kept.text: Independently of the first-token test, is_dense_amx_page requires the page's last entry to sit inside the same range as its first entry (pg.at_offset(63) < range.tok_hi), so any page with a range boundary inside it (HW/SW boundary, branch point, or a query token before offset 63) is never dense and always goes to the dotter loop.
kept.evidence: `pg.at_offset(page::page_size - 1) < range.tok_hi &&` ... comment at the AMX return: "is_dense_amx_page proved that the page's last token is below range_hint->tok_hi, so the dotter's advance (kv_idx >= tok_hi below) could not have fired for this page either"
corrections: Precise wording: is_dense_amx_page requires the page's last entry (offset 63) to lie below the tok_hi of the range that contains the page's FIRST entry (range = the page_begin_hint passed by apply_page_range [self_attention.hpp:1471-1472, 1540-1541, 1610]); since ranges are contiguous [ranged_mask.hpp:222, 263-265] this means all 64 entries share one range. Any range boundary inside the page (HW/SW boundary at shard.last_token_ix+1 [ranged_mask.cpp:66-79; full.hpp:1926-1934], a branch point / edge end [full.hpp:2937-2942], or a query token at page offset 0..62, whose boundary lands at offset 1..63 [ranged_mask.cpp:42-46]) makes the predicate false. Two imprecisions: (a) a boundary between ranges with identical masks is merged away by finalize_ranges [ranged_mask.cpp:~137-142], so only boundaries that survive finalization (mask changes, or the later reconciliation split) count; (b) "always goes to the dotter loop" holds only for a page that apply_page_tok is called on; apply_page_range may skip the page earlier (workless-range dismissal [self_attention.hpp:1481-1487], query not visible [1512], sliding window [1515-1517]), and inside the dotter loop non-visible runs are jumped over [1799-1803].

Precise wording: is_dense_amx_page requires the page's last entry (offset 63) to lie below tok_hi of the range that contains the page's first entry (the caller passes page_begin_hint = find_range(page.at_offset(0)) [self_attention.hpp:1471-1472, :1760-1761]). Because page token ids are contiguous [kv_cache.hpp:1517-1519] and ranges are sorted and gap-free [ranged_mask.hpp:216-227], any mask-range boundary at an offset 1..63 of the page fails the test and the page falls through to the dotter loop [self_attention.hpp:1770]. A boundary in the finalized ranged_mask exists only where the (sw, hw) masks differ, since finalize_ranges merges adjacent ranges with identical masks [ranged_mask.cpp:132-139]: a query token at offset q < 63 always creates one (its bit is present at tokens <= q and absent at q+1.. [ranged_mask.cpp:42-48, :64-66]); a shard (HW/SW) event always creates one when any query is pending (sw_mask moves to hw_mask [ranged_mask.cpp:67-73]); a branch point creates one only when the masks of the two sides differ (a prefix-cache continuation with no queries on the parent edge and one traversed child can be one merged range). A query at offset 63 puts the boundary at the next page, so that page can be dense (the pending page at N mod 64 == 0; measured pending_amx_visits 6,912). "Goes to the dotter loop" means "does not take AMX"; the dotter loop may still skip entries or return with no work when the query does not see the range [self_attention.hpp:1800-1803, :1817-1820].

kept.text: An "empty" visit is the return {0, range_hint} after the dotter loop scored no entry, which happens when every entry of [begin, end) is in a range where the query is not sw_required (the loop jumps with i = page.offset_for(range_hint->tok_hi) - 1) or is outside the sliding window.
kept.evidence: `if (!query_visible) { i = page.offset_for(range_hint->tok_hi) - 1; continue; }` ... `if (relevant_k_tokens == 0) return {0, range_hint};` (stats branch: `return {range_hint, 0, attn_stats::path::empty};`)
corrections: An "empty" visit is the return {0, range_hint} (stats build: {range_hint, 0, attn_stats::path::empty}) taken after the dotter loop scored no entry. That happens when every index of [begin, end) was skipped by one of the two loop guards: the query is not visible for the entry's mask range (in a hardware-offloaded layer without a sliding window the test is sw_required; in a non-hardware or sliding-window layer it is visible = SW_REQUIRED or HW_AVAILABLE), in which case the loop jumps with i = page.offset_for(range_hint->tok_hi) - 1; or the entry is outside the sliding window. A degenerate third case is an empty interval (begin >= end), e.g. page.count() == 0.

An "empty" visit is the return {0, range_hint} [self_attention.hpp:1817-1820] (stats build: path::empty [tron-attn-stats self_attention.hpp:1918]) after the dotter loop scored no entry (relevant_k_tokens == 0). That happens when every entry of [begin, end) is either (a) in a range where the query is not visible to the CPU pass, where "visible" means sw_required(job_ix) on a non-sliding-window layer under FPGA attention, and visible(job_ix) = SW mask OR HW mask on a sliding-window layer or under CPU attention [:1406-1407, :1746-1747, ranged_mask.hpp:155-162] (the loop then jumps with i = page.offset_for(range_hint->tok_hi) - 1 [:1802]), or (b) outside the sliding window [:1805-1808]; it also happens trivially when [begin, end) is empty (page.count() == 0, or EAGLE begin = 1 on a page whose only entry is token 0 [:1731-1743]).

kept.text: A page fully owned by the card produces an empty visit only when apply_page_range did not dismiss it first: the page-level gate sees_page uses visible() (SW or HW bit), so card-owned pages pass it, and the dismissal `continue` needs both dismiss_workless_ranges (page_range.size() * items.size() >= 64) and the page inside one range, so small sections visit every card-owned page once per (query, kv head) and record it as empty.
kept.evidence: `const bool dismiss_workless_ranges = page_range.size() * items.size() >= 64;` ... `return run_visible_in_software ? range.any_visible(batch_queries) : range.any_sw_required(batch_queries);` ... `if (n_entries == 0 || (page_in_one_range && !flagged_has_work)) { page_end_hint = page_begin_hint; continue; }` ... `bool sees_page = page_begin_hint->visible(tok_ix);` where `visible` = `sw_mask().contains(job_ix.i) || hw_mask().contains(job_ix.i)`
corrections: In a hardware-attention layer without a sliding window (run_visible_in_software = false, self_attention.hpp:1406-1407), a page fully owned by the card yields an empty visit whenever apply_page_range did not dismiss it: the page-level gate sees_page tests visible() = SW bit OR HW bit (:1499; ranged_mask.hpp:155-157), and the offloaded queries hold the HW bit on card-owned ranges (ranged_mask.cpp:71-73), so such pages pass the gate; the dismissal `continue` (:1486-1489) requires both dismiss_workless_ranges = page_range.size() * items.size() >= 64 (:1416; otherwise flagged_has_work is forced true at :1425-1426) and page_in_one_range (:1483-1484). So a section with fewer than 64 (page, query) pairs visits every card-owned page once per (query in items, kv head) and apply_page_tok returns 0 relevant tokens (:1766-1767 query_visible = sw_required = false; :1802 skip to offset_for(tok_hi) - 1; :1815-1817), which the TRON_ATTN_STATS build (tron-attn-stats) tallies as path::empty (:1918, :1617); main 0a51385e95 has no such counter. Larger sections still produce an empty visit for a card-owned page that straddles a range boundary (page_in_one_range false).

A page whose ranges carry only the HW bit for a query reaches apply_page_tok and returns an empty visit unless apply_page_range dismissed it first. The page-level gate `sees_page` uses visible() (SW or HW bit) [self_attention.hpp:1499; ranged_mask.hpp:155-157], so card-owned pages pass it. The workless dismissal `continue` [:1484-1487] fires only when three things hold: `dismiss_workless_ranges` (page_range.size() * items.size() >= 64, :1416), the page lies inside one mask range (:1482-1483), and no query of the whole minibatch needs that range in software (`range.any_sw_required(batch_queries)`, :1417-1420). So in small sections every card-owned page in the section is visited once per (query that sees the page, kv head) and returns empty; in large sections a card-owned page is still visited when it straddles a range boundary or when another query of the batch needs the same range in software. Qualifiers: (a) this holds only in hardware layers without a sliding window (run_visible_in_software false, :1406-1407); in sliding-window or non-HW layers query_visible = visible() (:1746-1747) and the same page is real AVX/AMX work, not empty; (b) each page sits in exactly one section per kv head because finish_sw_plan assigns every relevant page, including zero-work ones, to a section [model.hpp:2734; common.hpp:879-889], and select_relevant_pages keeps card-owned pages because it tests visible() [model.hpp:2338]; (c) an empty visit is not free: the query's Q group is packed for AMX on its first page of the call before apply_page_tok is entered (:1532-1536); (d) "record it as empty" exists only on the PR #4596 branch (`return {range_hint, 0, attn_stats::path::empty}` [tron-attn-stats self_attention.hpp:1918], tallied at :1617); main 0a51385e95 returns `{0, range_hint}` (:1817-1820) with no counter; (e) when the whole batch has zero software work, finish_sw_plan returns before any section exists [model.hpp:2710] and no page is visited at all.

kept.text: Neither uses_hw nor the FPGA mode is read by is_dense_amx_page or by the AMX gate in apply_page_tok; uses_hw only flips run_visible_in_software, which changes query_visible from visible() to sw_required(), so the AMX kernel applies to every page the CPU is required to score in both modes, and the only other gate is the packed Q pointer (null when AMX is unavailable or the kill switch is set).
kept.evidence: `bool const run_visible_in_software = sliding_window_size < illegal_sliding_window || !uses_hw;` ... `const bool amx_on = amx_eligible && amx_attn_h128g4::available();` ... `if (amx_q_packed != nullptr && is_dense_amx_page(page, begin, end, query_visible, *range_hint, q_position, k_position, sliding_window_size))` — the predicate's parameter list has no uses_hw or pending
corrections: Neither is_dense_amx_page [self_attention.hpp:1601-1612] nor the AMX gate in apply_page_tok [1759-1762] reads uses_hw or the FPGA mode; inside apply_page_range, uses_hw is read only at the definition of run_visible_in_software [1406-1407], which is true for any sliding-window layer or when uses_hw is false. run_visible_in_software selects visible() (SW or HW mask) versus sw_required() (SW mask only) [ranged_mask.hpp:155-162] at three sites: the per-range dismissal test range_has_work [1418-1419], the initial query_visible [1746-1747], and its re-evaluation at range boundaries [1797-1798]. The AMX kernel therefore runs, in both modes, on every (query, page) pair that passes all of: compile-time shape eligibility [1757-1758], a non-null packed Q (null when amx_on is false, i.e. no AMX-BF16 or TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 [1436-1439, 1528-1535, amx_attn.cpp:61,76]), and the dense predicate: begin == 0 (EAGLE sets begin = 1 on the k_position == 0 page [1739]), end == 64, query_visible under the mode's mask, the whole page inside one mask range, and inside the sliding window [1609-1611]. Pages the CPU must score that fail the dense predicate (partial pages, pages split by a range boundary) take the AVX dotter; pages whose range is HW-only under FPGA attention are skipped by both paths [1800-1803].

Precise wording: (1) uses_hw is read once in apply_page_range, to set run_visible_in_software = (layer has a sliding window) || !uses_hw [self_attention.hpp:1406-1407]; that flag switches BOTH the workless-range dismissal (any_visible vs any_sw_required, :1418) and the per-query visibility (visible() vs sw_required(), :1746/:1797). In a sliding-window layer the CPU scores the visible set even under FPGA attention. (2) The "packed Q pointer" gate is amx_on = amx_eligible && available() [:1436-1440]; amx_eligible is compile-time (head_size 128, kv_mul 4, bf16 query scalar [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:159-164]) and the whole path exists only under TRON_AMX_DISPATCH; available() is false for TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1, missing CPUID AMX-BF16/AMX-TILE, XCR0 without tile state, or a failed arch_prctl [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:58-71]. (3) Outer per-(query,page) skips before apply_page_tok (page not seen by the query, page wholly outside the sliding window, EAGLE 1-token page) apply to both paths equally [:1498-1526]; EAGLE's begin=1 on the k=0 page [:1740-1743] makes that page fail begin==0 in both modes.

kept.text: For a decode query at flattened token t, tok_hi of the range that holds t is t + 1: build_edge_ranges closes the range above each query event at token_ix + 1 and then emits the range that covers token_ix with the query's SW bit set, so every entry at index <= t on the query's branch lies in a range whose tok_hi <= t + 1 and whose sw mask (or hw mask, after a shard event) contains the query.
kept.evidence: `token_id next(token_ix.i + 1); if (next < hi && ...) { token_range r(next, hi, ...); out.push_front(...); }` ... `if (pop_query) masks.sw_mask().insert(popped_query_ix.i);` ... `hi = next;  // token_ix is covered by the next range below.` ... `if (edge_lo < hi && ...) { token_range r(edge_lo, hi, masks.sw_mask(), masks.hw_mask()); ...}`; the walker pushes `query_stack.push_back({token_id(tokens.size() - 1), token_job_id(token_jobs.size() - 1)})`
corrections: Precise wording: the query's flattened index is tokens.size()-1 at push time, and the "[t+1, hi)" close at ranged_mask.cpp:42-49 uses the masks before q is inserted, so the range starting at t+1 (if any) lacks q and finalize_ranges (ranged_mask.cpp:131-137) cannot merge it with the range holding t. Ancestor-edge ranges hold q because child subtree masks are OR-ed into the parent before the parent's build_edge_ranges runs (full.hpp:2953 then :2937 on the parent's own ascent). The hw-mask case arises only when a shard event ties at or lies below t on the branch (ranged_mask.cpp:66-82); the later reconciliation at full.hpp:1938-1961 may move q back from hw to sw (query below hw_attn_engagement_point, or a causal tail above a multi-query entry's last_token_ix) but never removes q from both masks.

Precise wording: "For a decode query at flattened token t, the finalized range that holds t has tok_hi == t + 1. build_edge_ranges closes the range above each query event at token_ix + 1 [ranged_mask.cpp:45-49] before inserting the query's bit into sw_mask [:64-66], then sets hi = next [:83], so the range covering t ends at t + 1 (emitted either by a lower event's close or by the final range [:87-90]); when t is the last token of its edge (the steady-state decode case) no range above is emitted because next == hi. finalize_ranges keeps tok_hi == t + 1, because its merge requires equal masks [:133-135] and the range above t never holds t's job bit; the later HW-mask reconciliation only splits ranges or moves bits between sw and hw [full.hpp:1928-1965]. Every entry at index <= t on the query's branch lies in a range whose tok_hi <= t + 1 and whose sw or hw mask contains the query (ancestor-edge ranges carry it through `*p.masks |= *my_masks` [full.hpp:2953]). Which of the two masks holds the bit is not settled by the shard event alone: (a) a shard event at or below t on the branch moves the bit to hw [ranged_mask.cpp:67-71], including the tie case where the shard's DMA'd last token equals t (possible for a listener query on an all-ready, DMA'd edge, both events pop together [:37-38]); (b) after finalize, the reconciliation moves the bit back to sw for ranges where the query's position is below hw_attn_engagement_point() [full.hpp:1937-1950] and, for hw_plan entries with more than one query, for ranges at or above entry.last_token_ix + 1 [full.hpp:1953-1965]."

kept.text: Therefore a ready page with 64 live entries becomes dense for a decode query at t exactly when its last entry index p63 <= t and no other query token lies inside it, which under CPU attention gives floor(N/64) dense pages for a context of N tokens (the page's current text), and the page that gains its 64th entry at step N mod 64 == 0 is dense from that very step onward.
kept.evidence: `pg.at_offset(page::page_size - 1) < range.tok_hi` with tok_hi = (smallest query token index >= the page's first entry) + 1 by the `hi = next` recurrence; with one query at t per branch, at_offset(63) = t satisfies t < t + 1
corrections: A ready page with 64 live entries (page.count() == 64) is dense for a decode query at t exactly when its last entry p63 satisfies p63 <= t, no query token and no shard boundary event lies at any of its entries p0..p62 (an event at p63 itself does not break density), the query sees the page (query_visible), and the page is inside the sliding window (always true when sliding_window_size is INT_MAX). Under CPU attention (USE_HW_ATTN=0) no shard events exist, so for a context of N tokens a decode query sees floor(N/64) dense pages and N mod 64 tokens on the dotter loop; the page that receives its 64th entry at step N mod 64 == 0 is dense from that very step onward (the query is its own p63 and t < t+1). Under FPGA attention the shard event at the DMA-complete boundary (dma_last_rel) can also split a page's range and remove density.

A page is dense for a decode query at t exactly when: begin == 0 (EAGLE excludes the page holding position 0), page.count() == 64, the query is in the mask of the range that holds the page's first entry, that range's tok_hi is above the page's last entry (no range boundary inside the page: no other query token, no edge/fork boundary from a prefix-cache split, and under FPGA attention no shard DMA event), and the page's first key is inside the layer's sliding window. Under CPU attention, for a branch that is one contiguous edge chain with no fork inside its pages, this gives floor(N/64) dense pages at context N, and the page that gains its 64th entry at step N mod 64 == 0 is a pending page that is dense in the pending pass from that step onward. With a prefix-cache fork at position f inside a page, that page is not dense for any branch, and the divergent branch's pages start fresh at f (new KV book, entry 0), so its pages fill when (N - f) mod 64 == 0.

kept.text: The pending pass differs from the ready pass only in which page list it walks and when it runs: estimate_attention_work puts a page in pending_page_ixs when it holds a token whose KV is written this forward (token_jobs_do_kv), run_sections selects pending_kv_plan versus ready_kv_plan, and run_attention_job runs the pending pass after upstream_kvs_ready.wait(); the `pending` flag is not read by apply_page_tok or is_dense_amx_page.
kept.evidence: `if (token_jobs_do_kv[j]) pending_pages.insert(token_pages[token_jobs[j]]);` ... `auto const& plan = pending ? plan_state.pending_kv_plan[worker_ix] : plan_state.ready_kv_plan[worker_ix];` ... `outer_batch->upstream_kvs_ready[binding.kv_slot].wait();` then `run_sections<geometry>(..., uses_hw, true);`; the apply_page_tok call passes `page_begin_hint, sliding_window_size, run_visible_in_software, amx_qp` and no `pending`
corrections: The pending pass differs from the ready pass in which page list it walks, when it runs, and how it is accounted: estimate_attention_work puts a page in pending_page_ixs when it holds a token whose KV is written this forward (token_jobs_do_kv) [model.hpp:1791-1797]; run_sections selects pending_kv_plan versus ready_kv_plan [self_attention.hpp:1111-1112]; run_attention_job runs the pending pass after upstream_kvs_ready.wait() [self_attention.hpp:782-789]. Inside apply_page_range the `pending` flag is read only for the perfetto trace label [self_attention.hpp:1390] and the TRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS page-visit tally [self_attention.hpp:1563]; it is not passed to apply_page_tok [self_attention.hpp:1539-1541, signature 1709-1721] nor to is_dense_amx_page [self_attention.hpp:1601-1614], so the AMX-versus-AVX choice is the same predicate in both passes.

Precise wording: "The pending pass and the ready pass run the same code (apply_page_range -> apply_page_tok -> AMX-or-AVX choice); they differ in (1) which page list they walk (pending_page_ixs = pages holding a token whose KV is written this forward, per token_jobs_do_kv [model.hpp:1791-1797]; the two lists get separate per-worker sections in finish_sw_plan [model.hpp:2719-2735]), and (2) when they run (ready before, pending after upstream_kvs_ready[kv_slot].wait() [self_attention.hpp:777-789]). The `pending` bool is forwarded into apply_page_range [self_attention.hpp:1118, :1384] but is used there only for the perfetto section label [:1390] and the optional TRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS tally [:1563]; it is not passed to apply_page_tok [:1539-1541] and is_dense_amx_page has no such parameter [:1601-1610]. A consequence for the AMX question: a pending page reaches the AMX kernel whenever its count() read at visit time (after the wait) is 64 and the other dense conditions hold [:1743, :1601-1614], which is what pending_amx_visits = 6,912 (the N mod 64 == 0 steps) shows."

kept.text: So the pending page (written in this forward) is dense and takes AMX when it is full, because end = page.count() = 64 and the query's own token at offset 63 satisfies at_offset(63) = t < tok_hi = t + 1; this matches the measured pending_amx_visits = 6,912 = 3 steps x 8 users x 36 layers x 8 KV heads at the steps where N mod 64 == 0 (counter name pattern "{pass}_{path}_visits").
kept.evidence: `size_t end = page.count();` ... `begin == 0 && end == page::page_size && query_visible && pg.at_offset(page::page_size - 1) < range.tok_hi`; stats: `"{}_{}_visits":{},"{}_{}_k_tokens":{},", pass_name, PATH_NAMES[p], ...` with pass = `pending ? attn_stats::PASS_PENDING_1 : attn_stats::PASS_READY_0`

Precise wording: for a decode forward carrying exactly one query per branch on the exact (non-EAGLE) scheduler, once the branch's first shard has passed the offload gate (>= 32 complete prefix GOFs, dma_last_abs >= hw_attn_engagement_point() = 127 unless USE_HW_ATTN=N raises it, shard not sw_fallback), the newest GOF that can be resident at plan time of query p ends at q = 4*floor(p/4) - 1: it fires in the forward of query q (the 8th K/V save credit, with earlier mates pre-credited), its DMA is submitted before that forward's logit delivery (wait_for_coop_gof), and its completion is only observed by poll_completions at the start of a later forward, so the earliest is the poll opening forward q+1. The CPU range is [dma_last+1, p] inclusive of the query, so cpu_tokens(p) = (p mod 4) + 1 + 4u, where u = number of GOFs in the shard chain from the first GOF not yet complete for every HW KV slot up to the GOF ending at q (with DMA holes, u also counts landed GOFs after the hole, because residency is a prefix count). u = 0 gives 1 to 4 CPU tokens; p = 1099 gives 4 tokens 1096..1099, matching the page's example only because 1099 mod 4 == 3. Below the offload gate the whole context is CPU work, and EAGLE branches are always CPU work.

corrections: Nothing in the scheduler bounds u (the in-flight GOF count). A GOF submission reserves the (GOF, slot) once (a dedup gate, shard.hpp:336-343), submits 36 descriptors, pushes a pending_xfer onto an uncapped priority queue and returns (model.hpp:3001-3019, dma_tracker.cpp:67-81). The one place a submitter waits on the card is DmaQueue::reserve_descriptor_slots_locked (dma_queue.cpp:354-390), reached under producer_mutex from xfer_n_blocks (driver.cpp:1188-1190); it stalls the submitting worker or forward thread until ring slots free, so it bounds outstanding descriptor slots on that device queue (32768 slots, common.hpp:33-37 and device.cpp:281-287, about 900 GOF submits est. at 36 descriptors per GOF, link slots ignored), not the number of GOFs missing from a plan. Other waits on the submit path (producer_mutex, the staging_busy CAS spin at gof.hpp:180-186, and the forward-end wait_for_coop_gof at model.hpp:1710/2900-2909) wait for other CPU threads to finish submitting, not for DMA completion. dma_tracker::await_slot (dma_tracker.cpp:135-148) is registered at model.hpp:1509-1510 but has no caller at 0a51385e95.

Claim is true as stated; add three qualifiers. (a) The backpressure loop is not an indefinite stall: after 2 x max_xfer_time_in_ns with no consumer progress it logs an error and calls tron::hardware::debug_exit, which terminates the process [src/pos/dma_queue.cpp:375-381]. (b) The ring bound is per DmaQueue: xfer_gof submits on dev->load_weight_q [src/tron/gof.cpp:178], so the descriptor budget is shared with weight-load DMA on that device queue, and the spin holds that queue's producer_mutex [src/pos/driver.cpp:1188-1189], which also blocks other submitters to the same queue. (c) A second blocking API exists, dma_tracker::await_slot [src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp:135-147], registered as the on_await_dma hook [h/tron/models/model.hpp:1509-1510], but nothing invokes on_await_dma at 0a51385e95, so it is dead code here; state this rather than "the only blocking point" without qualification. Optional: each in-flight GOF also holds DMA-heap staging buffers (K and V hwcacheblocks) until poll_completions frees them [h/tron/gof.hpp:216-235, src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp:115-123], so DMA-heap capacity is a memory bound on outstanding GOFs; whether exhaustion fails loud or blocks is Insufficient data (read the real dma_allocate_aligned).

The sw range for a decode query q is [dma_last_rel+1, q+1) (the query token included) [ranged_mask.cpp:42-49, :64-73], with dma_last = base_tok_ix + 4*complete_prefix_gofs - 1 and base_tok_ix a multiple of 1024 [full.hpp:2757-2759, :2792-2794, :2396], so it holds (p mod 4) + 1 + 4u tokens. A full page inside it needs at least 64 tokens (u >= 15, a lag of 60+ tokens) and is guaranteed only at 127 tokens (u >= 31); with small u every visited page runs the AVX dotter loop and card-resident pages are dismissed unvisited [:1416-1419, :1476-1486], which matches the page's "AMX gets no work in steady-state decode". Whole-shard software paths (first shard below hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload = 32 GOFs or below the 127 engagement point, a middle shard not dma_complete, a leaf shard with 0 complete GOFs, sw_fallback) put whole pages on the CPU and can take AMX [full.hpp:2750-2803; pos/config.hpp:98; libpos.hpp:90]. It consists of one "[attn-stats] model <id>: {summary JSON}" line (preceded by one empty line) and then, for each of the two classes decode_like and prompt_or_mixed, three lines: "[attn-stats] <class> totals: {JSON}", "[attn-stats] <class> forwards: {JSON}" and "[attn-stats] <class> k_tokens per layer (amx/avx/fpga): 0=A/B/C 1=A/B/C ...", so a runbook can use grep '^\[attn-stats\]' on stderr.

The stderr report is printed when a model state is destroyed, but only if TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 was set and at least one forward or page visit was counted (a state that never ran a forward prints nothing) [attn_stats.hpp:313-315, 653-666]. One report is seven lines: one "[attn-stats] model <id>: {summary JSON}" line, then for each of the two classes (decode_like, prompt_or_mixed) a "totals" line, a "forwards" line and a "k_tokens per layer (amx/avx/fpga): 0=A/B/C 1=A/B/C ..." line (A and B = ready + pending software K tokens summed over workers, C = FPGA K tokens) [attn_stats.hpp:668-688, 103-106]. The report is preceded by one blank line; grep '^\[attn-stats\]' still catches every report line. runtron builds one model state per prompt batch, so a multi-batch run prints one report per batch (per the author's comment, attn_stats.hpp:59-62 and README.stats.md:254-256). An EAGLE draft state shares the target's model id and prints its own report; the summary JSON's "eagle" field tells them apart [attn_stats.hpp:264, 579-583].

kept.evidence: "K tokens are counted per visit, once per kv head, so the number of dot products is k_tokens times the number of query heads per kv head (kv_mul)." ... "one pass serves all n_kv_heads of a query at once, so these K tokens compare with the software k_tokens (counted once per kv head) after multiplying by n_kv_heads" ... fc.token_jobs.fetch_add(n_token_jobs, ...);
corrections: The closest available measure of the CPU-scored K-token count per decode query under AoF is an average, not a histogram: (decode_like ready_avx_k_tokens + pending_avx_k_tokens + ready_amx_k_tokens + pending_amx_k_tokens, read from the decode_like_totals leaf as an interval difference) divided by (decode_like token_jobs x n_layers x n_kv_heads). Software k_tokens are counted once per (query token, KV page, kv head) visit; an AVX visit adds the relevant K tokens of the page, an AMX visit adds 64 (one whole page), an empty visit adds 0. decode_like counts every forward whose token jobs all have a listener, so it also includes 1-token final prompt chunks and speculative verify steps. The card's side is fpga_k_tokens / fpga_query_passes = average K tokens the card scored per (pass, query), where the count is the device-local index + 1 of the pass's shards; a query with passes on several devices contributes one pair per pass, and fpga_k_tokens_x_kv_heads puts the value on the software (per kv head) scale.

The closest available measure of the CPU-scored K-token count per decode query under AoF is an average, not a histogram: (decode_like ready_avx_k_tokens + pending_avx_k_tokens + ready_amx_k_tokens + pending_amx_k_tokens) divided by (decode_like token_jobs x n_layers x n_kv_heads), which is the mean number of K positions the CPU scored per (decode query, layer, KV head), because software k_tokens are recorded once per KV head per visit on both the AVX and the AMX path (an AMX visit records 64). The amx terms are zero with the default engagement point (position 127) and a card lag below one 64-token page, but are non-zero when USE_HW_ATTN=N raises the engagement point to a page boundary, or when any other full page is left to the CPU. The card's side, fpga_k_tokens / fpga_query_passes, is the mean number of K positions programmed for the card per (pass, query, layer) at job preparation time; it is on the same per-position scale as the software mean, and a query with more than one pass per layer splits its positions across passes. decode_like includes every forward whose token jobs all have listeners (one generated token per user, but also 1-token final prompt chunks and speculative verify steps), and queries below the engagement point have no FPGA pass, so the mean covers all of them.

kept.text: Under FPGA attention, ready_empty_visits does not count the card-owned pages as a rule: when page_range.size() * items.size() >= 64, apply_page_range dismisses a page whose single range has no software-required query without calling apply_page_tok (no visit of any kind), so empty visits arise only for small sections or for pages that hold more than one range, and the ready pass sees AVX k tokens only when the software-required range starts in a page that was not written in this forward.

corrections: Precise wording: "Under FPGA attention (hw layers have no sliding window, self_attention.hpp:487-495, so range_has_work = any_sw_required, :1406-1420), apply_page_range dismisses a page without calling apply_page_tok when page_range.size() * items.size() >= 64 (:1416) and the page lies in one range (last entry < that range's tok_hi, :1481-1483) that no query of the batch requires in software (:1484-1486); empty pages are skipped too. Card-owned pages are still planned into sections (select_relevant_pages keeps hw-visible pages, model.hpp:2334-2350; assign_page keeps zero-work pages, common.hpp:879-889), so this dismissal is the only thing that removes them. Empty visits therefore arise (a) in small sections (product < 64; e.g. one user with ~18 pages per section), (b) for pages that hold more than one range, and (c) in large sections for a single-range page that some batch query requires in software while another query sees it only through the hw mask: the page gate admits it with visible = sw | hw (:1500) and apply_page_tok then finds sw_required false (:1728-1729, :1773-1779) -> 0 k tokens. Case (c) needs mixed sw/hw membership on one range within one batch (prompt_or_mixed forwards, or pages shared by users with different DMA progress); with one query per user and no shared pages it does not occur. With AMX on (amx_q_packed != nullptr, :1751), non-EAGLE (:1732), and ready pages holding 64 entries, the ready pass sees AVX k tokens only for a ready page that straddles the hw/sw boundary, i.e. only when the software-required range starts inside a page that was not written in this forward (a ready page fully inside the sw range is dense and takes AMX, :1601-1614)."

Under FPGA attention on a layer that uses the card (uses_hw and no sliding window), ready_empty_visits does not count the card-owned pages when a section is large enough: apply_page_range dismisses a single-range page with no software-required query in the minibatch without calling apply_page_tok only when page_range.size() * items.size() >= 64, where page_range is one worker's share of one kv head's pages of one minibatch. In a one-user decode minibatch (items.size() == 1) that needs 64 pages (4096 tokens) per section, so at prompt 1024 every card-owned ready page is one empty visit; in the 8-user measured runs the threshold is reached and card-owned pages are dismissed. Empty visits then arise only (a) in small sections, (b) on pages that hold more than one range (branch point or SW/HW boundary inside the page), or (c) on a single-range page shared by a software-required query and a card-owned query of the same minibatch (a query below hw_attn_engagement_point sharing prefix pages with a longer query; full.hpp:1940-1951 moves only the short query's bits to sw). The ready pass sees AVX k tokens only when a software-required range (the tail above the last complete GOF, a short query's whole context, or a sw_fallback shard's range) starts in a page that no KV-writing token job of this forward touches; sliding-window layers score every visible token in software and are outside this statement.

kept.text: ready_avx_full_page_visits and pending_avx_full_page_visits count AVX visits that scored all 64 tokens of a page (AMX-eligible volume the AMX path did not take), so in an FPGA-attention run amx_visits = 0 together with avx_full_page_visits = 0 in decode_like means no full software page existed for the decode queries, while amx_visits = 0 with avx_full_page_visits > 0 would mean a full page existed but failed is_dense_amx_page or AMX was off.

corrections: ready_avx_full_page_visits and pending_avx_full_page_visits count AVX visits whose relevant_k_tokens equalled page_size (64): the page had 64 entries and every one was software-required for that query and inside the sliding window, which is exactly the token set the dense AMX kernel would have scored. In an FPGA-attention run, amx_visits = 0 together with avx_full_page_visits = 0 in decode_like means no (query, page, KV head) visit of a decode forward scored all 64 tokens of a page in software; it does not by itself say whether physically full pages existed, since a full page whose tokens the card owns records path::empty or a partial AVX visit. amx_visits = 0 with avx_full_page_visits > 0 means such full software visits existed but the AMX gate (packed Q present AND is_dense_amx_page) was false: the page failed is_dense_amx_page (for example it spans a range boundary, or was written in this forward), or AMX was unavailable/disabled (TRON_AMX_DISABLE, no AMX on the CPU), the geometry was not eligible, or the build lacked TRON_AMX_DISPATCH.

ready_avx_full_page_visits and pending_avx_full_page_visits count AVX visits whose relevant_k_tokens equalled 64: all 64 tokens of the page were software-required (sw_required under FPGA attention, visible under CPU attention) for that query and inside its sliding window. Such a visit exists only when (a) the page spans a query-mask range boundary (the one is_dense_amx_page sub-condition the AVX loop can pass with 64 tokens), or (b) no packed Q existed: AMX off (TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1), CPU/OS/permission refused, geometry not eligible (head 128, kv_mul 4, bf16 Q), or the build lacks TRON_AMX_DISPATCH. So, for an AMX-eligible geometry in a decode-only forward (decode_like = every token job has a listener), amx_visits = 0 and avx_full_page_visits = 0 mean no page with 64 software-required, in-window tokens existed for those queries; amx_visits = 0 with avx_full_page_visits > 0 means such pages existed and either spanned a range boundary or AMX was unavailable. Pages not counted by either leaf can still exist (EAGLE's first page scores 63 tokens; a full page partly outside a sliding window; pages skipped before apply_page_tok), and none of them is AMX-eligible. Decode queries inside a mixed batch are tallied under prompt_or_mixed, not decode_like.
