synth.verdict_on_user_impression: Short version: the AVX/AMX split of one decode query across the partial page (AVX) and the full pages (AMX) is a CPU-attention fact, not a steady-state FPGA-attention fact; under FPGA attention the AMX path still runs, but only in bounded non-steady cases, and no measurement has yet counted it there. Words used here: AMX = the dense-page kernel that scores one full 64-token KV page per call; AVX = the dotter loop that scores single entries; the pending page = the page written in this forward; a ready page = a page written in an earlier forward; a dense page = a page that passes is_dense_amx_page; the card = the FPGA; GOF = a group of four consecutive tokens, the unit of KV DMA to the card; HBM = the card's memory; the engagement point = the lowest query position the card may serve (127 by default). Under CPU attention (USE_HW_ATTN=0) a decode query at context N (tokens including itself) visits floor(N/64) ready pages on AMX and the N mod 64 tail tokens of the pending page on AVX, and at the steps where N mod 64 == 0 the pending page itself is dense and takes AMX [self_attention.hpp:1609-1611, :1743]; the 2026-09-24 counters confirm this (ready_amx_visits 10,278,144, pending_avx_visits 580,608, pending_amx_visits 6,912). The AMX gate reads neither uses_hw nor the FPGA mode: the same predicate runs in both modes, and the only extra input is which mask the query is tested against [self_attention.hpp:1406-1407, :1746-1747, :1759-1762]. Under FPGA attention the CPU is required to score only the tail above the card's boundary L, which is [L+1, p] inclusive of the query [ranged_mask.cpp:42-49, :64-73; model.hpp:2519]. When the DMA keeps up, L = 4*floor(p/4) - 1 and the tail is (p mod 4) + 1 = 1 to 4 tokens [full.hpp:2757-2759, :2791-2794; gof.hpp:34], so no full 64-token page is CPU work and no AMX visit occurs; the full pages below L are the card's, not AMX's, and the partial page is scored on AVX only for its tail. So the first half of the impression ("partial page split between AVX and AMX") describes CPU attention only. The second half ("AMX is still used on some decode tokens under AoF") is right in these cases, all read from code and none yet counted: a query below the engagement point (positions 64..126 give one dense page), a sequence whose first shard does not yet have 32 DMA-complete GOFs (fresh prompt, or a prefix-cache branch whose backfill has not landed), a DMA lag of 64 tokens or more (the code sets no bound), a sw_fallback shard after HBM exhaustion (the whole 1024-token range and everything after it is CPU work), a not-DMA-complete middle shard for contexts above 1024 tokens, and layers that never use the card (sliding window, EAGLE; not qwen-3-4b per the page). Note USE_HW_ATTN=1 keeps the engagement point at 127, the same as the default; only N >= 128 raises it [hw_attn_config.cpp:21-30; libpos.hpp:77, :90]. Evidence status: the steady-state "no AMX" statement is verified in code for a tail shorter than 64 tokens and is otherwise unmeasured; the 2026-09-17 EXE.AMX_BUSY count (501 M busy cycles under FPGA attention) proves AMX instructions ran in that cell but cannot say in which phase or through which case. The TRON_ATTN_STATS run under FPGA attention (decode_like ready_amx_visits, pending_amx_visits, and the fpga+amx / fpga+avx+amx path sets) is the measurement that settles it.
synth.steady_state_decode_aof: Short version: in steady-state decode under FPGA attention the card scores positions 0..L, the CPU scores L+1..p (1 to 4 tokens when DMA keeps up), and the CPU part never contains a full page, so every CPU visit is an AVX tail visit or an empty visit. Words used here: p = the decode query's 0-based position; L = the last position the card reads, fixed once per forward; a shard = a 1024-token region of HBM; kv_slot_extent = the number of KV slots (one per layer, 36 for qwen-3-4b if every layer is a hardware slot) whose DMA must land before a GOF counts. Step 1, the poll: at the top of forward(), before the plan is built, dma_tracker::poll_completions marks each landed GOF DMA done; this is the only place DMA completion is observed [full.hpp:1877-1878, :1893; model.hpp:1511; dma_tracker.cpp:108-109]. Step 2, the boundary: the tree walk reads count_complete_prefix_gofs(), the leading run of GOFs landed for every KV slot (a hole stops the count), and pushes the shard event at dma_last_abs = base_tok_ix + complete_prefix_gofs*4 - 1 [shard.hpp:355-364; full.hpp:2757-2759, :2791-2794]. So L is always of the form 4k - 1 [gof.hpp:34-36]. Step 3, the masks: build_edge_ranges closes the range [L+1, p+1) with the query in the software mask, then moves the query's bit to the hardware mask for every range at or below L [ranged_mask.cpp:42-49, :64-83]. Step 4, the plan: construct_hw_plan caps the card's range at min(p, L), which is L for a decode query [model.hpp:2510-2519]. The query's own K/V is written after the plan, so its GOF is never complete at plan time [full.hpp:1893, :1993; model.hpp:1706]. Step 5, the CPU pass: pages fully owned by the card are dismissed before apply_page_tok when the section has at least 64 (page, query) pairs, and otherwise visited and returned as empty visits [self_attention.hpp:1416-1420, :1481-1488, :1817-1820]. The page holding the boundary fails is_dense_amx_page on two conditions at once (the first-token range is the card's range, so sw_required is false; and that range ends inside the page) and the dotter loop scores only the tail entries on AVX [self_attention.hpp:1609-1611, :1746-1747, :1793-1808]. Step 6, the arithmetic: with DMA keeping up, L = 4*floor(p/4) - 1 and the CPU tail is (p mod 4) + 1 tokens, 1 when p mod 4 == 0 and 4 when p mod 4 == 3, mean 2.5 (est.); each GOF fired but not landed at the poll adds 4 tokens, and a hole adds every landed GOF after it too. Because L + 1 is a multiple of 4 and page starts are multiples of 64, the tail lies inside the pending page, so ready_avx visits are 0 and every CPU-scored token is a pending-page AVX token (est., DMA keeping up). Step 7, the GOF pipeline: a GOF fires when its 4 tokens' K and V saves reach 8 credits, i.e. in the forward whose query position q has (q+1) mod 4 == 0 [gof.hpp:343-355; full.hpp:2717-2727]; its DMA is submitted by an attention worker between layers (budget 4 per job) or by the forward thread in wait_for_coop_gof before logits [self_attention.hpp:731; model.hpp:1706-1717, :2895-2910]; its completion is first countable at the poll that opens the next forward [dma_tracker.cpp:83-129]. Nothing in the scheduler bounds the number of un-landed GOFs; the only wait is DMA descriptor-ring backpressure, which bounds descriptors, not GOFs [dma_queue.cpp:354-380; self_attention.hpp:666-671]. Preconditions for this picture: p >= 128 (the earliest query that can offload, because GOF 31 completes only after token 127's K is saved) [full.hpp:2756-2764; config.hpp:98], the first shard hw_usable (no sw_fallback) [shard.hpp:275-277, :356], and a layer that uses the card [self_attention.hpp:487-495]. Whether DMA keeps up on delphi-3bda is timing the code does not fix: Insufficient data; the decode_like ready_avx_k_tokens + pending_avx_k_tokens divided by (token_jobs x 36 layers x 8 KV heads) in a TRON_ATTN_STATS run under FPGA attention gives the measured mean tail.

cases.name: Query below the engagement point (positions 64..126 by default; wider when USE_HW_ATTN=N >= 128)
cases.phase: decode of a context shorter than 127 tokens; prefill only when a forward's queries start at a position in 64..126 (a prefix-cache hit or a chunk boundary there); NOT chunk 1 of a fresh 128-token prefill, whose page 0 is a pending page with one range per token and takes AVX
cases.when: query_pos < hw_attn_engagement_point(); the point is 127 by default, stays 127 for USE_HW_ATTN=1..127, and is max(127, ((N+128)/128)*128 - 1) for USE_HW_ATTN=N >= 128 (N=128 -> 255, N=1024 -> 1151). Queries at 0..63 have no complete page below them, so only positions 64..126 give AMX work at the default point.
cases.cpu_scores: every key 0..p on the query's branch: construct_hw_plan skips the query and the scheduler moves its bit from the hardware mask to the software mask in every range
cases.amx_runs: yes: page 0 (positions 0..63) is a ready dense page, 1 AMX visit per (query, layer, KV head); with a raised engagement point every ready full page below the query, floor(p/64) visits; the pending page stays AVX
cases.mechanism: `if (query_pos < hw_attn_engagement_point()) continue;` [model.hpp:2518] and `range.sw_mask() |= bits; ... range.hw_mask().erase(job_ix);` [full.hpp:1940-1948]; the page then passes `begin == 0 && end == page::page_size && query_visible && pg.at_offset(63) < range.tok_hi` [self_attention.hpp:1609-1611]. In steady-state decode past the engagement point this case contributes nothing.
cases.evidence_status: verified in code; not measured (no measured cell had decode queries below 127)
cases.measurement_that_settles: TRON_ATTN_STATS run with a prompt shorter than 64 tokens under FPGA attention: decode_like token_jobs_by_path_set 'amx' or 'avx+amx' > 0 for the steps at positions 64..126 while fpga_queries stays below token_jobs; or USE_HW_ATTN=1024 at prompt 1024 (point 1151): decode queries 1024..1150 must print 'avx+amx'.

cases.name: Sequence not yet engaged: query at or above 127 but the first shard has fewer than 32 DMA-complete GOFs (fresh prompt; the 128-token prefill forward 2; first decode steps of a short prompt)
cases.phase: prefill forward 1 (no AMX: every page is pending, AVX only); prefill forward 2 when any of the 32 GOFs x kv_slot_extent slots of tokens 0..127 has not landed at forward 2's poll (2 ready pages on AMX); decode when the context crosses 128 tokens before the 32 GOFs land
cases.when: count_complete_prefix_gofs() < hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload (32 GOFs = 128 tokens), or dma_last_abs < the engagement point (one GOF of lag at forward 2 gives 123 < 127), or dma_last_abs below the edge start: no shard is pushed, no hw_plan_entry exists, every query stays in the software mask
cases.cpu_scores: everything, the same split as CPU attention
cases.amx_runs: every ready full page below the query: for forward 2 of a 128-token chunked prompt 2 pages (0..63, 64..127) per (query, layer, KV head) = 2 x 128 x 36 x 8 = 73,728 visits per user; the own chunk (pending pages) stays AVX
cases.mechanism: `if (complete_prefix_gofs >= hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload) { ... if (dma_last_abs < tron::hw_attn_engagement_point()) { f.shard_push_stopped = true; break; } ... } else { f.shard_push_stopped = true; break; }` [full.hpp:2755-2779]; without a shard pop build_edge_ranges only runs `masks.sw_mask().insert(popped_query_ix.i);` and emits the final range with the software mask [ranged_mask.cpp:64-66, :86-90]. The earliest query that can offload is p = 128, because GOF 31 (positions 124..127) completes only after token 127's K is saved and completion is observed at the next forward's poll [full.hpp:1877-1893; model.hpp:1706].
cases.evidence_status: verified in code; whether the 32 x kv_slot_extent DMAs land before forward 2's poll is timing: Insufficient data. The 2026-09-18/19 CI cells (10.5 G AMX-busy cycles in 20 s with 4 short fresh requests under FPGA attention, 0 on the no-AMX package) are consistent with this case but do not isolate it.
cases.measurement_that_settles: prompt_or_mixed token_jobs_by_path_set 'avx+amx' > 0 together with fpga_queries < 7168 (8 users x 7 card-assisted chunks) in the FPGA-attention stats run; interval reads of the FUSE leaf between chunks give it per forward.

cases.name: Prefill pages not yet resident: chunk k >= 3 with a DMA lag of g GOFs while the first shard's prefix is still >= 32 GOFs
cases.when: at forward k's poll the leading complete run ends at dma_last_abs = 128(k-1) - 1 - 4g; the card scores 0..dma_last_abs; the lagging 4g tokens plus the own chunk are software work. A whole 64-token page takes AMX only if it lies entirely above dma_last_abs, which needs 4g >= 64 and page alignment; with g < 16 the lagging chunk contributes 0 AMX pages and only a partial AVX visit. At k = 2 any lag drops to the previous case (all-CPU, 2 AMX pages).
cases.cpu_scores: the lagging 4g tokens (from ready pages) plus the own-chunk causal triangle (pending pages, AVX)
cases.amx_runs: one AMX visit per (query, layer, KV head) for each whole ready page inside [dma_last_abs+1, 128(k-1)-1]; the page that straddles dma_last_abs is entered with the card's range as hint, fails the dense test, and the dotter scores its lagging tail on AVX after the skip to tok_hi
cases.mechanism: `bool query_visible = run_visible_in_software ? range_hint->visible(job_ix) : range_hint->sw_required(job_ix);` [self_attention.hpp:1746-1747] and `if (!query_visible) { i = page.offset_for(range_hint->tok_hi) - 1; continue; }` [self_attention.hpp:1800-1803]; the software range above the shard event is closed by `token_range r(next, hi, masks.sw_mask(), masks.hw_mask());` before the masks move [ranged_mask.cpp:42-49].
cases.evidence_status: verified in code; frequency of the lag state: Insufficient data
cases.measurement_that_settles: prompt_or_mixed ready_amx_visits > 0 with path set 'fpga+avx+amx' (whole lagging pages) and ready_avx_visits with ready_avx_k_tokens / ready_avx_visits < 64 (straddling pages) in the FPGA-attention stats run.

cases.name: DMA lag of a whole page in steady-state decode (u >= 15 fired-but-unlanded GOFs)
cases.when: the CPU tail (p mod 4) + 1 + 4u reaches 64 tokens or more with a whole 64-aligned page inside it: u >= 15 (a lag of 60+ tokens, 64 at least for the page to fit), guaranteed at u >= 31. Holes count: an un-landed GOF puts every landed GOF after it on the CPU too, because residency is a prefix count.
cases.cpu_scores: positions L+1..p, where L is the end of the leading complete run at the poll
cases.amx_runs: one AMX visit per whole ready page inside the tail; the straddling page and the pending page stay AVX
cases.mechanism: the code fixes no lag: submits push a pending_xfer and return [model.hpp:3017-3020], the plan never waits [self_attention.hpp:666-671 'No explicit await on KV DMA here'], on_await_dma is registered but never invoked [model.hpp:1509-1511], and the one blocking point is `while (!descriptor_capacity_available_locked(needed))` in the DMA descriptor ring, which bounds descriptors (32768 slots per queue, about 900 GOF submits est.) rather than GOFs missing from a plan [dma_queue.cpp:354-380; driver.cpp:1188-1192].
cases.evidence_status: predicted possible from code; Insufficient data on whether it ever happens (it needs about 60 decode steps of DMA lag, est., since one GOF fires every 4 steps per user)
cases.measurement_that_settles: decode_like ready_amx_visits > 0 with path set 'fpga+avx+amx' and fpga_queries = token_jobs in the FPGA-attention stats run; the ratio (ready_avx_k_tokens + pending_avx_k_tokens) / (token_jobs x 36 x 8) gives the mean tail; a perfetto trace of xfer_gof end versus the next poll_dma_completions gives the lag directly.

cases.name: HBM exhaustion at shard construction: the sw_fallback (degraded) shard
cases.phase: both; the effect covers the shard's whole 1024-token range and everything after it in that subtree
cases.when: at shard construction alloc_kv_weights returns an address that kv_weights_addr_valid rejects for the K or the V region (64 KiB each, 8 x 8192 B) of any hardware-eligible KV slot; the loop stops at the first failure, the driver prints 'HBM bypass space exhausted; caller degrades to SW attention', the constructor frees what it obtained, increments dev->sw_fallback_total once per degraded shard, and prints 'shard base tok_ix {} on dev {}: HBM exhausted ... {} of {} slots lose HW attention'
cases.cpu_scores: every token from the degraded shard's base_tok_ix onward (its 1024 tokens plus all later shards), and the whole context when it is shard 0, because hw_usable() gates both count_complete_prefix_gofs() (returns 0) and dma_complete() (returns false), so the shard is never pushed and stops the chain
cases.amx_runs: every ready full page in that range: the same split as CPU attention (floor(N/64) AMX pages plus the N mod 64 AVX tail per query, per layer, per KV head)
cases.mechanism: `if (!kv_weights_addr_valid(dev, k_base)) { sw_fallback = true; break; }` [gof.cpp:70-74]; `dev->sw_fallback_total.fetch_add(1, ...)` [gof.cpp:99]; `if (!hw_usable()) return 0;` [shard.hpp:356]; `if (!hw_usable()) return false;` [shard.hpp:402]; the first-shard else branch and the partial-leaf branch then set shard_push_stopped [full.hpp:2776-2779, :2802-2803]. The counter is exported at /rinzler/stats/memory_pressure/hbm/<dev>/sw_fallback_total [rinzler.cpp:4270-4271].
cases.evidence_status: verified in code; whether it occurred in any measured cell: Insufficient data
cases.measurement_that_settles: read sw_fallback_total per device during the run (nonzero = at least one degraded shard) and grep the rinzler log for 'lose HW attention'; in the stats run the affected requests print decode_like path set 'avx+amx' with fpga_queries below token_jobs, and their counters have the CPU-attention shape.

cases.name: Degraded shard persists on the tree edge and is inherited by later requests until a retry rebuilds it
cases.when: shards are owned by the token-tree edge, not the request, so every later request whose path passes that node sees the degraded shard; it is retried only from the dirty-edge path (the edge gained tokens or its KV was invalidated), only when a device passes the capacity gate (free bytes >= shard_hbm_bytes and largest free block >= 64 KiB), and only if the replacement itself comes out hw_usable; a stable ancestor edge is never swept and stays on software attention until it goes dirty again
cases.cpu_scores: as in the sw_fallback case, for every request through that node
cases.amx_runs: as in the sw_fallback case: every ready full page in the degraded range takes AMX
cases.mechanism: 'A stable ancestor edge holding a degraded shard is not swept, and stays on software attention until it goes dirty again' [full.hpp:2423-2426]; `n->remove_shard(shard_base); } n->add_shard(sh); tron::hardware::backfill_shard(sh, n, *state.dma_tracker);` with the log 'HBM available again, rebuilt with HW attention' [full.hpp:2504-2510]; 'Shard lifetime is tied to the token-tree edge, not to the request that used it' [shard.hpp:8]; the descent pushes `for (auto& si : edge.edge_shards())` of every ancestor edge [full.hpp:2747-2748].
cases.measurement_that_settles: the log line 'HBM available again, rebuilt with HW attention' after a 'lose HW attention' warning, and sw_fallback_total not increasing while the edge stays stable.

cases.name: Prefix-cache hit whose divergence lies inside a shard's 1024-token range (open): the new branch re-creates and backfills its own shard
cases.phase: the new request's first forward (prefill of its un-cached tail) and its early decode steps
cases.when: the new request matches a cached prefix but branches inside a shard's range (for a repeated prompt, the branch point is where the earlier request's generated tokens start). node::split_edge keeps on the shared edge only shards that end at or before the split and moves a spanning shard to the old child; the new branch's dirty edge finds no shard with that base (find_or_create_shard searches only its own edge), creates a 'leaf trailing' shard, and backfill_shard re-DMAs the shared-prefix GOFs that are fully saved (save_count >= 8) into that one shard. Until 32 complete GOFs of the new shard have landed at a poll, no hw_plan_entry exists and the whole prefix is software work; then the boundary L rises as the backfill lands. Sub-case: a divergence exactly at a shard boundary, or on an ancestor edge, reuses the earlier request's shards with no new DMA and is card-assisted from the first forward.
cases.cpu_scores: until engaged: every key; then L+1..p with L rising from 127 toward the prefix end
cases.amx_runs: until engaged: every ready full page below the query (14 pages for a 910-token cached prefix, est.); then each whole ready page inside the shrinking tail; the tail-writing pages stay AVX
cases.mechanism: 'A shard entirely before split_abs goes to intermediate; anything that reaches split_abs or beyond goes to child.' [full.hpp:1046-1048]; `for (auto const& sh : edge.shards) { if (sh->base_tok_ix != shard_base) continue;` [full.hpp:2457-2458]; `find_or_create_shard(static_cast<uint32_t>(last_full_base), "leaf trailing");` [full.hpp:2537-2538]; backfill walks the ancestor GALs `for (auto n = shard_node->shared_from_this(); n && !n->tree_is_root(); n = n->tree_parent())` [gof.cpp:235-236] and skips GOFs with `save_count < 2 * gof_tokens` [gof.cpp:259]; the first-shard gate then applies as in the not-engaged case [full.hpp:2755-2779].
cases.evidence_status: code path verified; which path a given cell takes (tree shape: split point versus shard range) and how many forwards the backfill of 228 GOFs x kv_slot_extent takes: Insufficient data. The 2026-09-17 cell (same prompt repeated, cached_tokens 910, branch inside shard 0) has this shape.
cases.measurement_that_settles: enable the commented-out 'allocating {} shard base' debug line (full.hpp:2493-2496) or trace backfill_shard events; in the stats run the request's first forwards print path sets 'amx' / 'avx+amx' (no card pass), then 'fpga+avx+amx' (card pass plus AMX pages inside the tail), then 'fpga+avx'.

cases.name: Context longer than 1024 tokens: a middle shard not DMA-complete, or a spanning shard whose DMA has not reached the edge
cases.phase: both (prompt 8192 cells; decode past 1024 tokens is the normal partial-leaf case and gives no AMX by itself)
cases.when: a non-first shard is pushed at its full extent only when dma_complete() (all 256 GOFs x kv_slot_extent landed); a non-first shard that is not complete is pushed at its DMA progress only if it has >= 1 complete GOF and its dma_last_abs reaches the edge start, and in every case the chain stops after it, so every later shard is software work; a spanning first or leaf shard whose dma_last_abs is below the edge start is not pushed
cases.cpu_scores: from the first unpushed position to p
cases.amx_runs: every ready full page in that range
cases.mechanism: `} else if (sh.dma_complete()) {` [full.hpp:2780] and `if (complete_prefix_gofs >= 1) { ... if (dma_last_abs >= parent.abs_ht.i) { ... shard_stack.push_back(...); } } f.shard_push_stopped = true; break;` [full.hpp:2785-2804]; child frames inherit shard_push_stopped [full.hpp:2841].
cases.evidence_status: verified in code; frequency Insufficient data
cases.measurement_that_settles: the same stats run at prompt 8192: prompt_or_mixed and decode_like ready_amx_visits with 'fpga+avx+amx' path sets.

cases.name: Layers or models that never use the card: sliding-window operations, EAGLE draft models, non-representable scale
cases.when: compute_operation_uses_hw is false (sliding window, EAGLE, scale mismatch), so run_visible_in_software is true and the CPU tests visible() (software OR hardware mask) instead of sw_required(); the CPU then scores every visible key on that layer whatever the batch's hardware plan holds
cases.cpu_scores: every key inside the window (or all keys) for every query
cases.amx_runs: every dense page whose first token is inside the window, every decode step; a window shorter than 64 tokens leaves no dense page; EAGLE's page 0 has begin = 1 and is never dense
cases.mechanism: `return ... hw_attn_eligible && ... .sliding_window_size == illegal_sliding_window;` [self_attention.hpp:489-494]; `bool const run_visible_in_software = sliding_window_size < illegal_sliding_window || !uses_hw;` [self_attention.hpp:1406-1407]; `run_visible_in_software ? range_hint->visible(job_ix) : range_hint->sw_required(job_ix)` [self_attention.hpp:1746-1747].
cases.evidence_status: verified in code; whether qwen-3-4b has any sliding-window layer is not readable from this tree (the page says none): Insufficient data
cases.measurement_that_settles: the per-layer line '[attn-stats] decode_like k_tokens per layer (amx/avx/fpga)': a layer with fpga = 0 and amx > 0 in a run where other layers have fpga > 0; or the ingested plugin's attention_operation_config.sliding_window_size.

cases.name: AMX tile instructions with no page visit: tile configuration and release per apply_page_range call
cases.when: whenever amx_on (AMX available and not kill-switched) apply_page_range runs begin_region() (LDTILECFG, loads the 8-tile configuration) at entry and end_region() (TILERELEASE) at every exit, once per call, dense page or not
cases.cpu_scores: unchanged; this is not a scoring path
cases.amx_runs: no dense-page kernel; two AMX instructions per apply_page_range call. This is not an 'AMX path' visit and TRON_ATTN_STATS cannot see it; it matters only for reading EXE.AMX_BUSY.
cases.evidence_status: call sites verified in code; whether EXE.AMX_BUSY (cpu/event=0xb7,umask=0x02) counts these two instructions: Insufficient data
cases.measurement_that_settles: perf stat of EXE.AMX_BUSY on the stats build under FPGA attention while the stats report prints ready_amx_visits = pending_amx_visits = 0; a nonzero busy count there is the per-call tile-config residual.

synth.table1_correction: Short version: no number replaces 0 in the steady-state FPGA rows, but the two FPGA cells must be re-labelled and get footnotes, because 0 is code-derived for a short tail only, was never measured, and is wrong for four whole-context software paths. Changes, cell by cell. (1) Decode row, FPGA attention: keep AMX = 0 pages and write the AVX cell as '(p mod 4) + 1 tokens = 1 to 4 tokens including the query, mean 2.5 (est., DMA keeping up), plus 4 tokens per GOF not landed at the poll'; replace 'lag 4 tokens (est.)' by 'tail 1 to 4 tokens (est.)', because 4 is the worst case of the keep-up range, not a constant [full.hpp:2757-2759; gof.hpp:34]. Write the card cell as 'positions 0..L, L = 4*floor(p/4) - 1 when DMA keeps up' and replace 'up to the last complete GOF' by 'up to the end of the leading run of DMA-complete GOFs at the poll that opens the forward' (a hole stops the run) [shard.hpp:355-364]. Label the row 'code-derived, est.; not measured under FPGA attention'. (2) Footnote A on that 0: 'holds while the CPU tail is shorter than one 64-token page; the code sets no upper bound on the DMA lag, so a lag of 64 tokens or more would put whole pages on AMX' [dma_queue.cpp:354-380; self_attention.hpp:666-671]. (3) Footnote B on that 0: 'under FPGA attention the following states give the CPU-attention split (floor(N/64) AMX pages + N mod 64 AVX tokens per query, layer, KV head) instead of 0: the sequence is not yet engaged (first shard below 32 DMA-complete GOFs, or the query below the engagement point, 127 by default), a sw_fallback shard after HBM exhaustion (its 1024-token range and everything after it), a prefix-cache branch inside a shard's range until its backfill lands, and a not-DMA-complete middle shard for contexts above 1024 tokens' [full.hpp:2749-2804; gof.cpp:70-103; full.hpp:1043-1054]. (4) Prefill row, FPGA attention: split it into 'forward 1' (AMX 0, AVX = own chunk, card 0: every page is pending, so this 0 is exact and does not depend on DMA) and 'forward k >= 2, DMA keeps up' (AMX 0 est., AVX = own chunk, card = 0..128(k-1) - 1). Footnote C: 'forward 2 sits exactly on the 32-GOF / 127 gate: one GOF of the 32 x kv_slot_extent (36 for qwen-3-4b) DMAs not landed at forward 2's poll makes forward 2 all-CPU with 2 AMX pages per (query, layer, KV head); at forward k >= 3 a lag of 4g tokens with the prefix still >= 32 GOFs puts each whole 64-token page inside the lag on AMX and the straddling page on AVX; a lag below 16 GOFs adds no AMX page' [full.hpp:2755-2779; config.hpp:98; self_attention.hpp:1609-1611]. (5) The row text 'positions below 127 are scored on the CPU only when the query itself is below 127' becomes 'positions below the engagement point (127 by default; USE_HW_ATTN=N >= 128 raises it to ((N+128)/128)*128 - 1) are scored on the CPU when the query itself is below the engagement point, or when no hardware entry exists yet for the sequence (fewer than 32 DMA-complete GOFs, sw_fallback shard), or on a layer that runs software attention for every query' [model.hpp:2511, :2518; hw_attn_config.cpp:21-30]. (6) The worked example 'here 1096, est. with a 4-token lag' is right as a token count (the card scores 0..1095 = 1096 tokens, the CPU scores 1096..1099 = 4 tokens) and only because 1099 mod 4 == 3; add 'for query 1096 the tail would be 1 token'. (7) Keep the CPU-attention row as is, with one addition: 'at the steps where N mod 64 == 0 the pending page is full and takes AMX (measured pending_amx_visits 6,912)'.
synth.interpretation_of_501M: Short version: the code settles that steady-state decode with DMA caught up produces no AMX page visit, so the 501 M busy cycles (57 % of the 873 M measured under CPU attention, one user, 3 decode-only requests after a warm-up with cached_tokens = 910, about 131 generated tokens each) must come from a non-steady path, from non-kernel AMX instructions, or from both; which one is Insufficient data, and the candidates are ranked below by how well the cell's shape fits them. Candidate 1 (most defensible, hypothesis): the prefix-cache branch inside shard 0. The repeated prompt matches the earlier request's edge and branches where the earlier generated tokens start, near position 910, which is inside shard 0's 0..1023 range; the spanning shard goes to the old child, the new branch creates its own base-0 shard and backfill_shard re-DMAs up to 228 GOFs x kv_slot_extent slots (est. 8208 GOF DMAs) [full.hpp:1043-1054, :2455-2462, :2525-2538; gof.cpp:227-289]. Until 32 of those GOFs have landed at a poll no hardware entry exists and the query scores all 14 full ready pages (floor(910/64)) on AMX; after that the boundary L rises from 127 as the backfill lands and every whole page inside [L+1, p] stays AMX [full.hpp:2755-2779; self_attention.hpp:1609-1611]. If that window covered roughly half of each request's 131 decode steps it would give a count of this order (est., not computed: the backfill duration is unknown). The stats run would print, for that request's early forwards, path sets 'amx' / 'avx+amx' (no card pass), then 'fpga+avx+amx', then 'fpga+avx'; decode_like ready_amx_visits > 0 and fpga_queries < token_jobs. Candidate 2 (hypothesis): a sw_fallback shard from HBM exhaustion on the new branch's shard allocation (each rebuilt shard takes 2 x 64 KiB per KV slot, 4.5 MiB est. for 36 slots), which makes the whole context CPU work for that request, i.e. the same AMX count per step as CPU attention [gof.cpp:70-103; shard.hpp:356, :402]. Two of three requests degraded would give about 67 %, one would give about 33 %; 57 % does not fit a whole number of requests unless mixed with candidate 1. The stats run would print decode_like path set 'avx+amx' for the affected request with fpga_queries below token_jobs, and sw_fallback_total > 0 at /rinzler/stats/memory_pressure/hbm/<dev>/sw_fallback_total [rinzler.cpp:4270-4271], with 'lose HW attention' in the log. Candidate 3 (hypothesis, least likely): a steady-state DMA lag of 64 tokens or more (u >= 15 un-landed GOFs, about 60 decode steps of lag, est.), which the code does not exclude [dma_queue.cpp:354-380; self_attention.hpp:666-671]. The stats run would print decode_like ready_amx_visits > 0 with path set 'fpga+avx+amx' and fpga_queries = token_jobs. Candidate 4 (hypothesis): the un-cached prompt tail. If the prompt was longer than 911 tokens, its tail was prefilled on the CPU with the 14 cached pages dense; with a 1-token tail (cached_tokens 910 of a 911-token prompt, est.) this is one forward and negligible; the prompt length of that cell is not in the evidence (Insufficient data). The stats run would show it in prompt_or_mixed ready_amx_visits. Candidate 5 (hypothesis): AMX instructions that are not page visits. begin_region/end_region run LDTILECFG and TILERELEASE once per apply_page_range call whenever AMX is available, dense page or not [self_attention.hpp:1457, :1460-1462; amx_attn.cpp:88-99]; whether EXE.AMX_BUSY counts them is Insufficient data, and if it does the busy count has a floor that no visit counter reports. Evidence against a large steady-state contribution: the 2026-09-19 perf record of an FPGA-attention decode run (VNNI-K build) showed the dense AMX kernel symbol absent while apply_page_range was present, which fits 'no dense-page visits in decode' for that run. The measurement that settles the 2026-09-17 cell: repeat it with the PR #4596 build (TRON_ATTN_STATS=1, USE_HW_ATTN default) and perf on the same pid, then read decode_like ready_amx_visits and pending_amx_visits, the token_jobs_by_path_set histogram, fpga_queries versus token_jobs, prompt_or_mixed ready_amx_visits, sw_fallback_total, and the rinzler log for 'lose HW attention' / 'HBM available again'; the per-forward view needs interval reads of the FUSE leaf /model/<id>/attention/decode_like_totals, since no per-step record exists [tron-attn-stats attn_stats.hpp:194-216, :437-451].
synth.fpga_run_expected_counters: Short version: for qwen-3-4b (36 layers, 8 KV heads), 8 users with fresh distinct prompts of 1024 tokens fed in 128-token chunks, 256 generated tokens, TRON_ATTN_STATS=1, USE_HW_ATTN unset, the steady-state prediction is decode_like ready_amx_visits = pending_amx_visits = 0 with every decode token job in the 'fpga+avx' set; each non-steady case has its own signature below. All values are est. from code unless marked measured. Baseline shape (measured under CPU attention on 2026-09-24, mode-independent per stats-8/9): decode_like token_jobs 2040 = 8 x 255 (queries at positions 1024..1278; the first generated token is counted in the prompt class), prompt_or_mixed token_jobs 8192 = 8 x 1024. Steady state, DMA keeping up: decode_like forwards line: fpga_queries 2040, token_jobs_by_path_set {fpga+avx: 2040, fpga+amx: 0, fpga+avx+amx: 0, amx: 0, avx+amx: 0}. decode_like totals: ready_amx_visits 0, pending_amx_visits 0, ready_avx_full_page_visits 0, pending_avx_full_page_visits 0; pending_avx_visits 587,520 (= 2040 x 36 x 8, one pending-page visit per query, layer, KV head, including the N mod 64 == 0 steps, whose full page fails the dense test because its head is the card's); pending_avx_k_tokens 1,465,344 (= sum over positions 1024..1278 of (p mod 4) + 1 = 636 per user, x 8 users x 36 layers x 8 KV heads), mean 2.5 tokens per visit; ready_avx_visits 0 and ready_avx_k_tokens 0 (the tail never crosses into the previous page when L + 1 is a multiple of 4); ready_empty_visits either 0 (card-owned pages dismissed, sections with >= 64 page x query pairs) or up to about 10.3 M (17.5 ready pages est. x 2040 x 288, every card-owned page visited and returned empty): the value itself tells which branch the decode sections take; fpga_k_tokens = sum over (query, layer) of L + 1 = about 84.4 M (293,124 per user per layer x 8 x 36); fpga_query_passes 73,440 (2040 x 36) if one pass per (query, layer), up to 146,880 if shard 0 and the leaf shard sit on two devices; fpga_k_tokens_x_kv_heads = 8 x fpga_k_tokens; join_wait_cycles > 0 (the streaming join is timed only when a hardware plan exists). prompt_or_mixed, DMA keeping up: token_jobs_by_path_set {avx: 1024 (chunk 1, no card pass), fpga+avx: 7168 (chunks 2..8)}, fpga_queries 7168, pending_avx_visits 3,538,944 (measured under CPU attention; mode-independent), ready_amx_visits 0, ready_avx_visits 0, ready_empty_visits 0 (128-query sections dismiss card pages); fpga_k_tokens per chunk k query = 128(k-1). Each un-landed GOF at a decode poll adds 4 x 288 = 1,152 to pending_avx_k_tokens per affected query, and once the tail crosses a page start it moves visits into ready_avx_visits with ready_avx_k_tokens / ready_avx_visits below 64. Case signatures: (a) query below the engagement point: absent in this cell (no decode query below 1024). (b) sequence not yet engaged (forward 2 of a user with any of 32 x 36 GOF DMAs not landed): prompt_or_mixed 'avx+amx' rises by 128 per such user-forward and fpga_queries falls by 128; ready_amx_visits rises by 73,728 (2 pages x 128 x 288) per such user-forward. (c) prefill lag at chunk k >= 3: prompt_or_mixed ready_amx_visits > 0 with 'fpga+avx+amx' (36,864 per whole lagging page per user-forward), ready_avx_visits > 0 with k_tokens per visit below 64 for straddling pages; the lag never touches decode_like. (d) DMA lag of a whole page in decode: decode_like ready_amx_visits > 0, 'fpga+avx+amx' > 0, fpga_queries still 2040. (e) sw_fallback shard: for each degraded user the decode_like line shows 255 jobs in 'avx+amx', fpga_queries = 2040 - 255 x (degraded users), ready_amx_visits about 17.5 x 255 x 288 = 1.28 M per degraded user (the CPU-attention shape: measured 10,278,144 for 8 users), pending_amx_visits 864 per degraded user (3 steps x 288), and sw_fallback_total > 0. (f) prefix-cache branch inside a shard: not expected with distinct fresh prompts; if the 8 prompts share a prefix (runtron -u with the same prompt), prompt_or_mixed token_jobs drops below 8192 (cached tokens are not token jobs) and the early forwards of later users print 'amx' / 'avx+amx' then 'fpga+avx+amx'; check the two token_jobs sums first (2040 and 8192) before reading the classes as decode steps and prompt forwards. (g) sliding-window layer: the per-layer line shows fpga = 0 with amx > 0 for that layer; not expected for qwen-3-4b. (h) tile config without visits: all amx visit counters 0 while perf EXE.AMX_BUSY on the same pid is nonzero. Reading rules: the counters are cumulative since the model state was built (runtron: one state per prompt batch), an interval is the difference of two FUSE reads, and the stderr report is one 'model' line plus three lines per class starting with '[attn-stats] ' [tron-attn-stats attn_stats.hpp:313-315, :668-688, :721-756].
contradictions_with_page: Page (b) 'est. 4-token lag' / Row B 'the CPU scores the remaining 4 tokens': the code gives a tail of (p mod 4) + 1 = 1 to 4 tokens including the query when DMA keeps up, plus 4 per un-landed GOF; 4 is the worst case of the keep-up range, and the example holds only because 1099 mod 4 == 3 (query 1096 would leave 1 token) [full.hpp:2757-2759, :2791-2794; gof.hpp:34; ranged_mask.cpp:42-49].

Page (b) 'up to the last complete GOF at plan time': the boundary is the end of the leading run of DMA-complete GOFs (complete for every KV slot); a GOF landed behind a hole does not count, so the boundary can sit below the last complete GOF [shard.hpp:355-364].

Page (b) 'no full CPU page exists, so AMX gets no work in steady-state decode': true only while the tail is shorter than 64 tokens; the code sets no upper bound on the DMA lag (no await, descriptor-ring backpressure bounds descriptors only), so the sentence must carry 'when the DMA lag stays below 64 tokens (not measured)' [dma_queue.cpp:354-380; self_attention.hpp:666-671; model.hpp:1509-1511].

Page (c) 'positions below 127 are scored on the CPU only when the query itself is below 127': three states are missing: no hardware entry exists yet for the sequence (first shard below 32 DMA-complete GOFs, or dma_last_abs below the engagement point), a sw_fallback shard, and a layer that runs software attention for every query (sliding window, EAGLE); also '127' is the engagement point, which USE_HW_ATTN=N >= 128 raises to ((N+128)/128)*128 - 1, while USE_HW_ATTN=1 leaves it at 127 [model.hpp:2511, :2518; full.hpp:2755-2779; shard.hpp:356; self_attention.hpp:487-495, :1406-1407; hw_attn_config.cpp:21-30; libpos.hpp:77, :90].

Page (c), boundary detail: a query at position 127 passes the query gate (127 is not below 127) but cannot offload, because GOF 31 (positions 124..127) completes only after token 127's K is saved and completion is observed at the next forward's poll; the earliest offloading query is p = 128 [full.hpp:2756-2764, :1877-1893; model.hpp:1706].

Page (d) Table 1 'AMX 0' in the FPGA prefill row with 'DMA keeps up (est.)': forward 1 is 0 exactly and independent of DMA (every page is pending); forward 2 sits exactly on the 32-GOF / 127 gate, so one un-landed GOF of 32 x kv_slot_extent makes it all-CPU with 2 AMX pages per query; the row must say which forward it describes [full.hpp:2755-2779; config.hpp:98].

Page (d) Table 1 'AMX 0' in the FPGA decode row: 0 is code-derived for a short tail and unmeasured; it is wrong for the not-engaged, sw_fallback, prefix-cache-backfill and not-DMA-complete-middle-shard states, where the row reads like the CPU-attention row; the 2026-09-17 501 M busy cycles show AMX ran under FPGA attention in one cell without saying where [gof.cpp:70-103; full.hpp:1043-1054, :2780-2804].

Page (a) / Row A 'the 12-token tail page (the pending page, written in this forward) takes AVX' is right for N = 1100 but incomplete as a rule: at the steps where N mod 64 == 0 the pending page is full and takes AMX (measured pending_amx_visits 6,912 = 3 steps x 8 users x 36 layers x 8 KV heads) [self_attention.hpp:1743, :1609-1611].

User's framing 'partial page split between AVX and AMX under AoF': under FPGA attention the full pages below the boundary are the card's, not AMX's, and the partial page contributes only its tail on AVX; the AMX/AVX split of one query is a CPU-attention fact [ranged_mask.cpp:64-73; self_attention.hpp:1746-1747].

User's framing 'USE_HW_ATTN is 1': USE_HW_ATTN=1 forces hardware attention on and keeps the engagement point at 127, identical to the unset default for qwen-3-4b; it does not raise the software window [hw_attn_config.cpp:21-30].

Internal conflict among kept claims, resolved per Rule 7: dense-13's correction says USE_HW_ATTN=128 gives 191 and the point rises to k*64-1; plan-8 says 255 and ((N+128)/128)*128 - 1 with POS_PER_PAGE = 128; the code has `static const size_t POS_PER_PAGE = 128;` [libpos.hpp:77] and `pages * POS_PER_PAGE - 1` [hw_attn_config.cpp:29-30], so plan-8 is right and dense-13's numbers must not be used.

Internal conflict among kept claims, resolved per Rule 7: prefill-4's second correction says the prefill chunk is 1024 tokens for ingested plugins (live_token_limit), while prefill-1 says 128 tokens per forward (TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT default 128, libtron.hpp:196-204) and the measured prompt_or_mixed pending_avx_visits 3,538,944 = 192 x 8 forwards x 8 users x 36 x 8 and path set {avx: 1024} = 8 x 128 forward-1 jobs reproduce only with 128-token chunks; use 128 (the scheduler's live_token_limit is an upper bound the 128-token chunk never reaches).

findings.text: Case 7 (prefix-cache branch) and candidate 1 of the 501 M interpretation say the boundary L 'rises from 127 toward the prefix end as the backfill lands'. The code does not do that. The first shard on an edge is pushed only when its DMA-complete prefix reaches the edge's first position: `if (dma_last_abs < parent.abs_ht.i) { f.shard_push_stopped = true; break; }`, where `parent` is `*edge.parent` (the node at the edge's start) [full.hpp:2766-2771, :2206-2208]. A branch edge that starts at position 910 therefore needs 228 complete GOFs (dma_last_abs = 911) before any hardware entry exists, not 32. GOF 227 (positions 908..911) belongs to the new edge's GAL and fires only when token 911's K and V are saved, in the branch's second forward; its completion is first seen at the third forward's poll [gof.hpp:47-49, :343-355; gof.cpp:235-262; full.hpp:1877-1893]. So the branch runs all-CPU for at least two forwards (every ready full page on AMX: 14 pages for a 910-token prefix, per layer and KV head) and then switches to card-assisted in one step, with no intermediate state. Three texts must change: (a) case 7's 'Until 32 complete GOFs ... then L rises' and 'each whole ready page inside the shrinking tail'; (b) the stats signature in case 7, in candidate 1 and in signature (f): no 'fpga+avx+amx' phase exists, the sequence is 'amx' or 'avx+amx' for the un-engaged forwards and then 'fpga+avx'; (c) Table 1 footnote B: 'until the backfilled prefix reaches the branch point (at least 2 forwards)'. The same gate applies to the 8-user cell if the -u prompts share a prefix. Confidence: high (three code sites read).

Candidate 1 is ranked 'most defensible' with no magnitude check, and the sentence 'If that window covered roughly half of each request's 131 decode steps' has no backing claim. With the corrected mechanism (finding 1) the all-CPU window is at least 2 forwards per branched request. backfill_shard submits every GOF of the shared prefix synchronously inside the descent (228 GOFs x 36 slots = 8,208 transfers, est.), and the descriptor ring throttles submission to DMA completion: the ring has 32,768 slots (256 pages x 128 descriptors of 32 B in a 4,096 B page) and one GOF-slot transfer takes 36 descriptors, so about 910 transfers can be in flight and all but the last 910 have landed before forward 1's attention starts [gof.cpp:227-289, :155-159; dma_queue.cpp:354-380; dma/common.hpp:26-27, :35-36; device.cpp:284-285]. Estimated AMX visits from candidate 1: 2 to 3 forwards x 14 pages x 288 (36 layers x 8 KV heads) = 8 K to 12 K per request (est.), against about 131 forwards x 15 pages x 288 = 566 K per request under CPU attention (est.), about 2 %. A 57 % share needs a window of about 75 forwards, or a prefix that never completes (finding 3). The ranking must state this arithmetic and demote candidate 1 unless the backfill duration is measured (perfetto 'backfill_shard' event against the next 'poll_dma_completions').

Missing case: a hole in a backfilled prefix that never closes. backfill_shard skips a GOF when the slot's gof object is null (`if (!g) continue;`) or when `save_count < 2 * gof_tokens` [gof.cpp:251-259]. count_complete_prefix_gofs stops at the first GOF whose dma_done is below kv_slot_extent [shard.hpp:355-364]. If a skipped GOF lies below the branch point, the shard never passes the edge-start gate [full.hpp:2768-2771], and the whole branch (its prefill tail and every decode step) runs software attention with every ready full page on AMX. This is an all-or-nothing per-request outcome with the same shape as sw_fallback, but sw_fallback_total stays 0 and no warning is logged. Frequency: Insufficient data (the code read here does not say when gofs[slot] is null for a fully saved GOF). Signature: decode_like 'avx+amx' with fpga_queries = 0 for that request and no 'lose HW attention' line; a per-forward print of count_complete_prefix_gofs() settles it.

Case 9 (layers that never use the card) lists sliding window, EAGLE and scale mismatch, but the per-operation gate has more conditions: is_hardware_attention_candidate requires operation.hardware == kv_slot_candidate, writes_kv, no sliding window, kernel geometry equal to the bitfile geometry, and KV-slot geometry equal to the kernel's KV geometry [kv_cache.hpp:396-408]; configure_hw_attention sets the hardware bit only for such operations ('Other operations use software') and kv_slot_extent is the highest such slot index plus one [model.hpp:1445-1459]. A model-level gate (use_hw_attn_for_this_model: max_shards_for_emem == 0, or no devices) makes the whole model CPU attention [model.hpp:717-727, :1514-1533]. A per-layer software subset is the one mechanism that gives a constant fraction of the CPU-attention AMX work at every decode step, so it belongs in the 501 M candidate list with the per-layer '[attn-stats] ... k_tokens per layer' line as its test. For qwen-3-4b all 36 layers share one geometry, so it is all-or-nothing there (not verifiable from this tree: Insufficient data).

The synthesis reads the 2026-09-19 perf record (dense AMX kernel symbol absent, apply_page_range present) as fitting 'no dense-page visits in decode'. That reading is weaker than stated. apply_dense_amx_page is declared TRON(inline), which expands to `inline __attribute__((always_inline))`, so it never has a symbol of its own; only the kernels in amx_attn.cpp can appear in a profile [attributes.hpp:75-78; self_attention.hpp:1623-1625]. The run was a VNNI-K build, whose K-side kernel differs from main's, and perf sampling cannot exclude a 1 % to 3 % share (the candidate-1 magnitude of finding 2). Write it as 'consistent with, not proof of', and name the symbol that was searched.

Fairness of the verdict. It says the non-steady cases are 'none yet counted'. The 501 M EXE.AMX_BUSY cycles are a count of AMX activity in a decode-dominated FPGA-attention cell whose shape (same prompt repeated, cached_tokens 910) is the prefix-cache branch of case 7, and the kill-switch arm gave 0. So the user's second claim ('AMX is still used on some tokens' decode attention under AoF') is measured true for that cell, and the code names the path; only the share per path is open. The verdict should say that plainly. It should also say that the user's first claim (a partial latest page splits the work between AVX and AMX) describes the software path, which runs in both attention modes whenever the CPU scores the whole context (not engaged, degraded shard, branch before its prefix lands), rather than calling it a 'CPU-attention fact' only.

Case 1 says 'Queries at 0..63 have no complete page below them, so only positions 64..126 give AMX work'. At p = 63 the pending page 0..63 is full and dense: end = page.count() = 64, the query event closes the range at tok_hi = 64, and at_offset(63) = 63 < 64, the same mechanism as the measured 6,912 pending AMX visits [self_attention.hpp:1743, :1609-1611; ranged_mask.cpp:42-49, :86-90]. At p = 127 the query passes the gate (127 is not below 127) but no shard exists yet, so page 0 (ready) and page 1 (pending, full) both take AMX, one visit each per layer and KV head. The range should read 63..127 with both endpoints explained, and the case-1 measurement line should include positions 63 and 127.

Steady-state Step 7 says 'the only wait is DMA descriptor-ring backpressure, which bounds descriptors, not GOFs'. That is literally right but misleading. One GOF-slot transfer takes 36 descriptors (4 K blocks + 32 V blocks) and the ring has 32,768 slots, so the ring bounds in-flight transfers to about 910 per device, which is about 25 token-GOFs (100 tokens, est.) for one user on one device [gof.cpp:155-159; dma/common.hpp:35-36]. That bound is above the 64-token page threshold, so the lag case (case 4) stays possible; say so instead of 'no bound'.

Case 4 says a whole page is 'guaranteed at u >= 31'. A tail of (p mod 4) + 1 + 4u tokens contains a whole 64-aligned ready page for every alignment only from 127 tokens, so the guarantee is u >= 32 when p mod 4 == 0 (u = 31 gives 125 tokens, which can miss the page); u >= 31 holds only when p mod 4 == 3.

The 57 % ratio compares two runs of 'about 131 generated tokens each'. The exact per-request token counts are not in the evidence, so the ratio carries the length difference between the runs. State the uncertainty, or cite the exact counts from the two runs' usage fields.

Case 6 sub-case 'a divergence exactly at a shard boundary, or on an ancestor edge, reuses the earlier request's shards with no new DMA' holds only for shards whose range ends at or before the split (shard_end <= split_abs); the shard that spans the split always moves to the old child, and children_shards on the ancestor are used only to wire GOF DMA targets, never for the shard push [full.hpp:1046-1054, :2878-2889; token_tree.hpp:301-312].
